earlier_scan.source_named: Jackson, Bruce; Jackson, Andy; Lau, Shuh Huey. 2012. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Dejing Zhuang Dialect Area (SIL ESR 2012-036) — phonological notes on Yang Zhuang; sil.org returns 403

sources.citation: Jackson, Eric. 2019. Two-Part Negation in Yang Zhuang. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society (JSEALS) 12(1): 52-82. hdl:10524/52443 (CC-BY).
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Nothing. Syntax paper on Jingxi county-seat Yang; sec. 1 lists the descriptive literature (Zheng 1996 = lexicon, phonology and basic syntax of county-seat Yang; Huang 2010 MA grammar; Qin, Huang & Chen 2010 on negation); footnotes note tone sandhi (high falling realised high level before a high tone) and glottal tension on tone C1. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Jackson, Eric M., Emily H.S. Jackson & Shuh Huey Lau. 2012. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Dejing Zhuang Dialect Area. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-036. 168 pp.
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.3.2 (pp. 12-14) summarises published phonologies (preglottalized-stop/nasal merger, tone-value differences) and sec. 4.2 'Wordlist results: Tone systems' compares Gedney-chart tone categories and phonetic tone values at 18 datapoints; grep stress/unstress/accent/promin returns only sociolinguistic 'prominent' and RTT-participant 'stress'. No word-stress statement. (sil.org direct = Cloudflare 403; fetched sources from web.archive.org snapshot 20230403102804.)

sources.citation: Johnson, Eric C. 2011. A Lexical and Phonological Comparison of the Central Taic Languages of Wenshan Prefecture, China. SIL Electronic Working Papers 2011-005. 171 pp.
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative phonology (tones, consonants, vowels) of Nong, Dai and Min Zhuang of Yunnan; Jingxi and Debao Yang Zhuang appear only as comparison datapoints (lexical-similarity table p. 7; shared A1 tone-split pattern, sec. 3.3). No stress/prominence statement for any variety (grep = 0 relevant hits).

sources.citation: Lee, Sampson. n.d. Yang Zhuang 佒壯語 documentation (orthography notes: initials, rimes, tones). https://abcsampson.github.io/YangZhuang/documentation
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States that most Yang Zhuang dialects have a 6-tone system derived from an earlier 3-tone system by a split according to initial phonation; tense/lax vowel distinction affects tone in checked syllables; Guiliu Mandarin loans carry four extra tones.
